cityOwner: 00/03 City Service Network — Capability Registry & Discovery
adaptation: CommonJS -> ESM JavaScript, and TypeScript -> ESM JavaScript. No donor code is executed: a provider's effect is supplied by the caller as `execute`, because a module in this tree must not run another project's code.

The donor's `register` allowed a second owner to claim a capability and only refused at resolution time. This module refuses at registration instead, naming the mistake where it is made; re-registration by the same owner is still an update.
`revoke(capabilityId, owner)` is added beside the donor's `revokeOwner(owner)` and returns the removed provider record, so a caller can report what went away.

The donor's `provider-contracts.ts` `AdapterOutcome` and `provider-outcome.ts` `NON_SEMANTIC_RUNTIME_CODES` were two separate vocabularies of the same thing; they are one vocabulary in `contracts.mjs`.

The donor's `detectGoalDrift` inlined its bilingual scope-change markers; they are extracted into the exported `SCOPE_CHANGE_MARKERS` table so the phrase data is visible and extendable without editing the algorithm.

The donor's `capability-router.ts` classified by `ModuleState`. Utopia's City manifest declares lifecycles, so `moduleStateForLifecycle` maps the manifest vocabulary onto the donor's states and `bridgeStateForLifecycles` reproduces the exact derivation the accepted Utopia V0.3 registry used.

A module reference the manifest does not name resolves to `UNKNOWN` (bridge state BRIDGE_PENDING) rather than the donor's `UNAVAILABLE`, because 'the map does not list this' is not the same claim as 'a deprecated owner withdrew it'. The V0.3 registry derived the same bridge state for this case.

The donor's health supervisor restarted a plugin through `manager.reload`. Here the ledger counts the attempt and reports the reaction; the caller performs the reload. The restart budget is still consumed before the attempt, as in the donor.

The lock document is JSON rather than the donor's YAML-shaped line format, because the donor's parser refused every deviation it did not understand and JSON gives the same strictness with no hand-written parser to drift. The strict rules are preserved: version shape, id shape, an owner per entry, absent-is-not-drift, refuse-to-write-empty, sorted rendering.
knownDifferences: No file hashing anywhere in the lock, exactly as in the donor: DS-Hns `app/core/lockfile/index.cjs` imports no crypto at all and compares `id -> version` strings only. No digest verification was invented.

The Hns plugin/adapter/installer platform is deliberately NOT migrated: plugin-adapters (format detection, adapter registry, compatibility), plugin-compat, plugin-install, config-manager and the permission/host layers belong to 01/01 Customs (MB-011), 01/02 Runtime Compliance (MB-012) and 02/02 Worker Gateway (MB-003).

The Hns 30-name capability vocabulary in `contracts/capability.cjs` is product vocabulary (`computer-use`, `ui-stability`, `long-term-worker`, `dshns.*` provider ids). Only its *shape* — a closed vocabulary with a documented fallback per capability — is carried; the City declares its own capability names.

Codex-Boss `electron/capability/capability-broker.ts`, `authorization.ts` and `permission-contract.ts` are NOT migrated: they are the admission/authorization seam owned by MB-011/MB-012. The broker's `describes`-must-be-present rule and its 'no handle without a decision' property are preserved in this module's own terms (a provider must describe itself; the only way to reach a provider is `invoke`, which checks availability and the operation allowlist first).

There is no provider-discovery module, because the donor has none: the Boss 'discovery' vocabulary is repository/workbook discovery. Provider observation in the donor is `RuntimeRegistry.refreshHealth` and account/model probing, the latter being Electron-bound; this module's health probing covers the reusable half.

Codex-Boss `src/shared/provider-capabilities.ts` (the per-provider boolean capability profile with `canHandleObject` / `withinUploadLimit`) is NOT migrated: it exists to route *file attachments to web AI panes*, which is provider-window product behaviour, not city-global capability metadata.
Codex-Boss `src/shared/capability-gap.ts` is NOT migrated: its durable writer is the Boss engineering improvement loop, which is Engineering self-improvement and belongs to the Engineering Missions.

No persistence: the registry, the ledger and the invocation history are in memory, as in the donor's registry. `lock.mjs` is the only module that touches the filesystem, and it touches exactly one file.

vectors: resolution is by capability name, never by provider identity
a second owner claiming a capability is refused with the owners named
the same owner re-registering its own capability is an update, not a conflict
a missing required capability is recorded as a miss and names the requester; an optional miss is recorded without a fault
unloading an owner revokes every capability it provided, and a later miss says REVOKED rather than MISSING
a provider that does not state what invoking it can do is refused
the lookup log is bounded and a read cannot mutate the registry
installed/enabled/loaded/healthy stay four independent facts with a derived label in a fixed order
a disabled provider is refused a load unless forced; a second load is already:true
a throwing health probe is UNHEALTHY and never escapes
an unasked or unparseable health answer is UNKNOWN, never HEALTHY
the health reaction order is healthy, unknown, fatal, soft, then the restart budget
the aggregate verdict is blocked on a fatal fault, degraded on any unhealthy provider, healthy otherwise
a runtime-layer fault classifies UNCLASSIFIED with confidence 0, runtimeAttributable true and penalizesSemanticProfile false
an explicit refusal inside a successful call is HARD_REFUSAL with penalizesSemanticProfile true
deterministic verification and format failures outrank provider-behaviour signals
an unobservable success is UNCLASSIFIED rather than a fabricated completion
goal drift is reported with its evidence and the goal is never rewritten
an evaluator revision is appended and the original evaluation is preserved
provider lifecycle is WAITING_PROVIDER (autoResume true) or PAUSED_PROVIDER (autoResume false); an unknown action is ACTIVE
an undefined retryAt is absent from the record, not zero
a capability whose owner is not PROMOTED/ACTIVE answers BRIDGE_PENDING and runs nothing
a deprecated owner makes the capability UNAVAILABLE
an operation outside the provider's allowlist is OPERATION_BLOCKED before any work runs
a completed invocation carries a digest of its canonical result
an unknown throw becomes ADAPTER_UNAVAILABLE and a typed error survives
a result over the size bound is refused as RESULT_TOO_LARGE
concurrency is bounded and a busy capability answers BUSY
an in-flight invocation becomes INTERRUPTED with GATEWAY_RESTARTED after a restart, and is not left RUNNING
a ranking may reorder the approved candidates, cannot add one, and a throw leaves the deterministic order untouched
drift is an exact owner/version set diff with added, removed and changed named
an absent lock is not drift; an empty lock is refused; enforcement is opt-in; an unparsable lock is invalid

PARITY: resolution by capability with priority order
four independent lifecycle facts with the derived-state order
health reaction ladder and bounded restart budget
ranking may only reorder the approved set
lock set-diff drift with absent-is-not-drift and refuse-empty
PORT_ADAPTATION: registration-time ownership refusal instead of resolution-time
provider effect injected by the caller
City lifecycle vocabulary mapped onto the donor's routing states
UTOPIA_EXTENSION: one capability vocabulary instead of the donor's two
a provider ledger whose reload is performed by the caller
DEFERRED: plugin/adapter format detection and the adapter registry (MB-011 Customs)
permission and authorization resolution (MB-012 Runtime Compliance)
Engine provider planning, session registries and the learning loop
